title: Protecting Cyber-Physical Systems via Vendor-Constrained Security Auditing with Reinforcement Learning
problem: CPS security requires vendor diversity for mutual auditing against hardware Trojans, but multi-vendor integration creates cost and maintenance challenges with insufficient vendor availability.
motivation: Trustworthy CPS requires hardware security while minimizing vendor diversity constraints and operational complexity.
method: The system audits devices to detect when hardware Trojans (malicious circuits hidden in chips) from different vendors coordinate, then removes infected devices from operation. It employs multi-agent reinforcement learning (multiple AI agents learning through trial and error) to automatically decide which vendor should supply each device, optimizing to keep the maximum number of devices running.
key_novelty: Using multi-agent reinforcement learning to assign devices to vendors protects cyber-physical systems from hardware Trojans even when only a few vendors are available.
contributions: Vendor-constrained auditing framework for CPS with untrustworthy devices
Side auditing mechanism for Trojan collusion detection
40.95% reduction in vendor requirements with 0.39% infected node increment
baselines: mutual auditing framework without RL optimization
limitations: Evaluation limited to hardware Trojan scenarios; generalization to other CPS threat models not discussed.
primary_theme: RL-based CPS security auditing with vendor constraints
